drivingQuestion: Why does Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel hold that returning the deed returns the gift?
outcomeNote: Rav Asi's reason is attacked in the next unit

segments.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַנּוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ, וְהֶחְזִיר לוֹ אֶת הַשְּׁטָר – חָזְרָה מַתְּנָתוֹ. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מַתְּנָתוֹ קַיֶּימֶת. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, נַעֲשָׂה כְּאוֹמֵר לוֹ: שָׂדֶה זוֹ נְתוּנָה לְךָ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהַשְּׁטָר בְּיָדְךָ.
segments.en: § The baraita teaches that «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:» In the case of «one who gives a gift» of land «to another, and» the recipient «returned the deed to him, his gift» of land «returns» to him as well. «But the Rabbis say: His gift» of land «remains» in the possession of the recipient. The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» for the opinion «of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel? Rav Asi says: It becomes as» if the giver «said to» the recipient: «This field is given to you» only «as long as the deed» remains «in your possession.» Therefore, by returning the deed to the giver, the recipient is canceling the gift.
